topics.display_title: Effects of Globalisation on Indian Society

panels.title: Globalisation channels
ascii_lines: ENTRY -> consumer markets, urban labour migration, food industry, digital access
SOCIETY LAYER -> identity, household authority, work patterns, information access
EXCLUDED -> trade and investment macroeconomics owned by Economy
EXCLUDED -> labour codes and gig-work law owned by Social Justice
MUST REMEMBER: Globalisation intensifies cross-border flows of capital, goods, services,
people, information and culture, producing glocalisation, consumption change, labour-market
restructuring, care chains, diaspora networks and uneven bargaining power.

panels.title: Consumer culture in two layers
ascii_lines: STRUCTURAL -> market access, purchasing capacity, retail expansion, credit
CULTURAL -> status signalling, brand identity, aspiration
ORDER -> the structural layer can precede and outlive the cultural one
USE -> concede consumption precisely, then refuse the exclusivity claim
source_references: Consumer culture and its two layers

panels.title: Convergence against adaptation
ascii_lines: HOMOGENISATION -> predicted convergence of brands, formats and consumption
GLOCALISATION -> observed adaptation of menus, language and platform content
STATUS -> one is a prediction, the other an observation
ERROR -> treating them as rival theories with one winner

panels.title: Domain matrix
ascii_lines: STRONG CONVERGENCE -> global brand recognition and shared media formats
STRONG ADAPTATION -> regional-language content and locally customised menus
RULE -> both processes run at once in different domains
ANSWER MOVE -> name the domain, do not deliver a single global verdict

panels.title: Labour evidence card
ascii_lines: PLFS 2023-24 -> released 23 September 2024, female LFPR 41.7 per cent
COMPARATOR -> 37.0 per cent in 2022-23, worker population ratio 40.3 per cent
PLFS 2025 -> released March 2026, usual-status female LFPR 40.0 per cent
CAUTION -> January to December 2025 period replaces the July to June cycle

panels.title: Evidence-strength ladder
ascii_lines: ESTABLISHES -> aggregate participation in the labour force
SUGGESTS -> the employment context of a migration decision
DOES NOT ESTABLISH -> size, age, marital status, destination or cause
PROHIBITION -> no migration stream may be inferred from a participation rate
source_references: What a participation rate cannot prove

panels.title: Freedom and renegotiation
ascii_lines: INCOME AND RESIDENCE -> mobility, spending autonomy, later marriage, partner voice
CONTINUING TIE -> remittance, ritual participation, periodic visits
WEAKENED -> day-to-day parental oversight
VERDICT -> coexistence and renegotiation, never severance
source_references: Family renegotiation and its security cost

panels.title: Freedom and security trade-off
ascii_lines: GAIN -> independent decision-making away from household supervision
COST -> thinner family support during harassment or health emergency
IMPLICATION -> workplace and housing safety become the binding constraint
ANSWER USE -> qualify the freedom claim instead of celebrating it
source_references: Family renegotiation and its security cost

panels.title: Fast-food paradox drivers
ascii_lines: TIME -> dual-income urban households face real constraints on home cooking
PRICE AND DELIVERY -> platform logistics lower the cost of convenience
ASPIRATION -> branded consumption signals urban modern identity
ADAPTATION -> locally customised menus widen the addressable market

panels.title: Behavioural lens card
ascii_lines: CLASSICAL PREDICTION -> rising health awareness reduces consumption
OBSERVED -> awareness and industry growth coexist
LENS -> bounded rationality weighs convenience and status against long-run health
LIMIT -> a lens, not proof that one motive dominates every purchase
CLOSE DISTINCTION: Globalisation is not westernisation, liberalisation is not privatisation,
cultural diffusion is not homogenisation, hybridity is not equal exchange, and aggregate
growth or connectivity does not establish inclusion, causation or uniform local response.
source_references: Bounded rationality and domestic food systems

panels.title: Digital access ladder
ascii_lines: ROUND SIX FACT SHEETS -> ever-internet use 64.3 per cent, women aged 15 to 49
ROUND FIVE COMPARATOR -> 33.3 per cent for the same measure
STATUS -> round six results are labelled provisional
DIVIDE -> access is unequal by income, gender, region and generation
EVIDENCE LIMIT: Use IT-Bengaluru, garment clusters, Kerala-Gulf migration, platform work,
food/media hybridity and farmer/artisan value chains with sector and region qualifications;
distinguish policy chronology, firm strategy, technology and household agency.
source_references: The digital-access anchor and its status

panels.title: Globalisation answer spine
ascii_lines: OPEN -> name the channels, refuse the single-force framing
BODY -> concede consumption, then add labour, family and digital channels
TEST -> convergence against adaptation, domain by domain
CLOSE -> graded verdict with the statistic and status caveats
source_references: Question ownership and the answer spine
